history.period: Modern (founded 2005; new monumental temple under construction)
history.summary: The ISKCON temple at Sagar Nagar, officially the Sri Sri Radha Damodar Temple, is the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) centre of Visakhapatnam, located on Hare Krishna Land on Beach Road near Rushikonda. It was founded in 2005 (on Akshay Tritiya, per travel guides) and enshrines milky-white marble idols of Krishna with his siblings Balaram and Subhadra, worshipped as Sri Sri Radha Damodara. The complex is a full spiritual centre with a temple hall, prasadam hall, ashram for resident monks, a vegetarian restaurant and a gift shop selling the Bhagavad Gita and Srila Prabhupada's literature; it runs kirtans, bhajans, spiritual lectures, yoga and meditation sessions and Vedic philosophy workshops, plus community food-distribution programmes. A monumental new temple building has been under construction at the site for several years.

name: ISKCON Temple
town_description: Visakhapatnam (Vizag), on the Bay of Bengal in coastal Andhra Pradesh, is the state's largest city and its main port, nicknamed the 'City of Destiny'. Known for Rushikonda Beach, RK Beach, Kailasagiri hill park and the ancient Simhachalam Narasimha temple, it is both an industrial and tourism hub. The ISKCON temple sits on Beach Road at Sagar Nagar, between the Rushikonda and Yendada stretches of the coast.

travel.airport: Visakhapatnam Airport (approx. 12-15 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Visakhapatnam Junction (approx. 10-12 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: On Beach Road at Sagar Nagar near Rushikonda; easily reached by city buses, autos and taxis from anywhere in Vizag.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when Vizag's weather is pleasant. Janmashtami is the most vibrant time to visit; Sunday feasts draw large devotee crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 7:30 AM to 12:30 PM; evening 4:30 PM to 8:00 PM, open all days (verify — one source lists 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM, another 4:30 AM to 8:30 PM). No entry fee; footwear not allowed inside.
